<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="סיון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518918964_theRebbe_845" batchId="meluket-_D7_A1_D7_99_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518918964_theRebbe_845__p001">

  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The verse about Aaron's staff blossoming almonds is explained in Likkutei Torah, where almonds symbolize speed, alluding to the swiftness of the priesthood's influence.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And behold, the staff of Aaron had blossomed... and produced almonds."</t>
    <t s="1">And it is explained in Likkutei Torah, in the discourse beginning with this verse,</t>
    <t s="2">that the reason it specifically produced almonds is that almonds ripen more quickly than any other fruit.</t>
    <t s="3">[And Likkutei Torah adds there,</t>
    <t s="4">that therefore they are called "shkeidim," from the term "shkidah," meaning haste and speed,</t>
    <t s="5">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="6">"a rod of an almond tree... for I am hastening (shokeid) My word to perform it."</t>
    <t s="7">And it can be said</t>
    <t s="8">that the intention of this addition is to hint that the speed inherent in almonds is their essential quality,</t>
    <t s="9">and as is known</t>
    <t s="10">that the name of a thing indicates its essence],</t>
    <t s="11">and therefore they allude to the priesthood,</t>
    <t s="12">because the influences drawn down through Aharon the Kohen</t>
    <t s="13">[Aharon — the letters spell "ra'ah" (seeing)]</t>
    <t s="14">are with speed.</t>
    <t s="15">And likewise, this applies to all the Kohanim, the sons of Aharon,</t>
    <t s="16">for when the Kohanim bless the people,</t>
    <t s="17">influence is drawn down below with great speed, without delays</t>
    <t s="18">(as will be explained in section 7).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The root of all influence is from the attribute of Chesed of Atzilus, which descends through the worlds, requiring daily judgment and prayer for it to manifest in physical matters.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="2">that the root of all influences is from the attribute of His kindness,</t>
    <t s="3">the Chesed of Atzilus.</t>
    <t s="4">And in order for physical influences—</t>
    <t s="5">children, life, and sustenance—</t>
    <t s="6">to be drawn from the Chesed of Atzilus, it is through the descent and progression of Chesed through all the levels from Atzilus to Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="7">And at every transmission from one level to the next, there is judgment and adjudication</t>
    <t s="8">as to whether the influence will be drawn into the lower level or remain in the higher level.</t>
    <t s="9">And this is why we pray and ask daily, "Heal us,"</t>
    <t s="10">"Bless upon us,"</t>
    <t s="11">even though a person's sustenance is fixed for him from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur</t>
    <t s="12">(and the intention here in "sustenance" includes all three matters: children, life, and sustenance),</t>
    <t s="13">because the writing and sealing for good on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is the drawing of Chesed into Malchus of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="14">and for the influence of Chesed to be in physical matters, it is through the descent and enclothing of the Chesed of Malchus of Atzilus into the Chesed of Beriah,</t>
    <t s="15">and afterward into the Chesed of Yetzirah and Asiyah.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is the meaning of "a person is judged every day,"</t>
    <t s="17">even though his verdict was already concluded on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="18">because the judgment on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur is that Chesed be drawn to the person in Malchus of Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="19">and the judgment in which a person is judged every day is</t>
    <t s="20">whether he is worthy that the Chesed already drawn upon his soul above on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur will descend and be drawn</t>
    <t s="21">(through Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah until it is drawn)</t>
    <t s="22">down into this physical world,</t>
    <t s="23">or whether the Chesed will remain above and additional delight will be added for him above.</t>
    <t s="24">Therefore we pray every day, "Heal us" and "Bless upon us," etc.,</t>
    <t s="25">that the Chesed allotted to him on Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur be drawn down into this physical world,</t>
    <t s="26">and within this world itself—into physical matters.</t>
    <t s="27">And there is another aspect to the daily judgment,</t>
    <t s="28">that since the Chesed above is spiritual Chesed,</t>
    <t s="29">even after the verdict that it be drawn down into this world,</t>
    <t s="30">there is judgment and adjudication regarding which specific matter the Chesed will be drawn into.</t>
    <t s="31">Therefore, they instituted praying every day the thirteen middle blessings, which include requests for all the needs of the individual and all the needs of the community.</t>
  </section>
